grammar.title: Talking about possibility with 可能 and 该
grammar.explanation: 可能 (kěnéng) means "maybe, possibly" and usually comes before the verb. 该 (gāi) means "should" and is a shorter, more casual version of 应该. Both are used to guess or to give soft advice.

grammar.title: Cause and effect with 因为...所以
grammar.pattern: 因为 + reason, 所以 + result
grammar.explanation: 因为 (yīnwèi) gives the reason and 所以 (suǒyǐ) introduces the result together they mean "because...so". Chinese usually keeps both words, even though English often drops "so".

sentences.zh: 因为下雨，所以我们没出去。
sentences.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒmen méi chūqù.
sentences.en: Because it rained, we didn't go out.

sentences.zh: 因为我很忙，所以没时间看电影。
sentences.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ méi shíjiān kàn diànyǐng.
sentences.en: Because I'm busy, I don't have time to watch a movie.

sentences.zh: 因为他病了，所以没上课。
sentences.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā bìng le, suǒyǐ méi shàngkè.
sentences.en: Because he was sick, he didn't go to class.

sentences.zh: 因为这本书很好，所以我买了。
sentences.pinyin: Yīnwèi zhè běn shū hěn hǎo, suǒyǐ wǒ mǎi le.
sentences.en: Because this book is good, I bought it.
Today isn't as hot as yesterday.
